source_state: Working tree based on baseline_commit with uncommitted compressor changes: sessions of unknown length infer C's UpdateSizeHint size hint before their first encode, sizing storage for the inferred total only for a body of at most 4 KiB finished in that call; the full QuickMatcher table (q2-q4, H54) is allocated by MatchFinder::materialize once the size is known; and the q5/q6 tagged bucket matchers that know their input sample the first block (greedy::probe::sample_store_outlook) to choose the dense table from 8/16 KiB for ordinary data and to keep repetitive data on demand. One-shot calls, which these sweeps time, reach the first and last changes. Decoder sources unchanged from baseline_commit.

corpus_generation: Eight inputs: empty, tiny-text, alice29, text-1m, binary-64k, random-64k, random-1m, repeated-1m, from the pinned core.rs generator (xorshift64 seed 0x243f6a8885a308d3; structured binary ((i/16)^i) mod 256; repeated a; cyclic Alice); streams produced by Google C at q0-q11, window 22.
limitations: One WSL2 host; frequency, thermals and host scheduling uncontrolled.
Fixed decoder order; confidence intervals capture sampling variation, not all environmental bias.
C receives known output capacity; Rust Vec APIs grow output during decode; Rust brotli includes 4 KiB I/O adaptation.
Only cold APIs and C-generated standard-window streams; no streaming, reuse or dictionaries. Historical timings are not paired before/after measurements.

Eight benchmark processes ran at once on separate cores and shared the last-level cache, memory bandwidth and the package's turbo budget; absolute timings are below a single-core sweep and latency cases of tens of nanoseconds (empty input) move most. Ratios to C are the comparable quantity.
No builds, tests or other benchmark processes ran on the host during the sweep.
timestamps_note: wall-clock date -u taken immediately before the eight lanes started and after the last one ended (encoder and decoder sweeps ran together)
